records.question: How long does Spotify hold on to my personal information?
records.text:
According to Section 6. Data retention, Spotify keeps personal data for as long as the user chooses, unless one of the limited purposes applies. 

* Data that expires after a specific period of time, for example, personal data you may input as part of search queries is deleted after 90 days.
* Data retained until your Spotify account is deleted, such as your Spotify username and profile information.
* Data retained until you remove it, as it's your right to request that Spotify delete certain of your personal data.

[Spotify – 6. Data retention]

records.question: Can other people read my Zoom Email messages?
records.text:
[Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?]
* **Zoom Email, Calendar and Zoom Team Chat Recipients:** Recipients of Zoom Emails and Zoom Calendar invites can see, save, and share your email and calendar content with others, including by sharing emails to Zoom Team Chat. If a recipient shares encrypted content with others, for example, by sharing an encrypted Zoom Email to Zoom Team Chat, or forwarding an encrypted Zoom Email to a third-party recipient without a Zoom Email account, the shared or forwarded content will not be end-to-end encrypted by Zoom. Those with access to your device and login credentials may be able to see, save and share your email and calendar contents on that device.

[Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?]
* **Limited Information from Zoom Email and Calendar Services:** “Zoom Email” refers to Zoom’s native email service and emails sent from Zoom’s native email service. Zoom Email is designed to be end-to-end encrypted by Zoom by default for emails sent and received directly between active Zoom Email users. Support for end-to-end encryption requires Zoom Email users to have added a device to their Zoom Email account with the associated email address and to use a supported Zoom client. When an email is end-to-end encrypted, only the users, and, depending on their settings, account owners, or designated account administrators control the encryption key and therefore access to the email content, including body text, subject line, attachments and custom labels applied to messages by users in their inboxes.

According to this, if you send an encrypted Zoom Email to someone, they can still share it with others without end-to-end encryption. However, if you send an email directly to another Zoom Email user, it is end-to-end encrypted by default.
cited_labels: [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?]
[Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?]
